public_rationale: The claim is about one session with the free version of ChatGPT on or about 4 February 2025. Marcus describes the session as lasting 10 minutes. The contract reads "count to 50" as meaning that answers meant to list all 50 states had a row count other than 50. The claim is supported only if the shared transcript, or an independent check of it, shows at least two such answers. The evidence includes neither the transcript nor such a check. A post by Benjamin Todd, available on 9 February 2025, says "GPT-4o misses out a bunch of states" (e1). It does not say whether Todd looked at Marcus's transcript. It also does not give a row count for any of Marcus's tables or say how many tables were wrong. A reader comment dated 5 February 2025 says the reader's own GPT-4o run left out states (e2). That was a different session. Neither item shows that two or more of Marcus's tables had a count other than 50.
limitations: The shared transcript linked in Marcus's post was not found, so the rows in his tables could not be counted.
e1 does not show whether its author checked Marcus's transcript, and it gives no row counts.
e2 describes a different session and cannot show what Marcus's session produced.
The contract notes that "count to 50" is figurative. Its reading as table row counts is an interpretation.
